title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Louisiana TANF

3 OUT OF 100

Poor Louisiana families who got cash aid in 2022-23. It was 48 in 1995-96.

Demand a real safety net in Louisiana.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Child poverty cost

CHILD POVERTY COSTS UP TO $1.1 TRILLION A YEAR

National Academies estimate. Ending it costs far less.

Tell Congress: invest in kids now.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Life expectancy

POOR WOMEN DIE 10 YEARS SOONER

Richest 1% vs. poorest 1% of American women. Poverty steals years.

Fight for health care and wages that keep people alive.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Food insecurity

47.9 MILLION. NOT ENOUGH FOOD.

People in food-insecure households, USDA 2024. In the richest country on Earth.

Protect SNAP and free school meals.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Kids and hunger

18.4% OF FAMILIES WITH KIDS COULDN'T COUNT ON FOOD

USDA, 2024. Hunger at the kitchen table, not on the news.

Fight for universal school meals in your district.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Evictions

2.7 MILLION HOUSEHOLDS HIT WITH EVICTION FILINGS

In a typical year. Eviction doesn't just follow poverty. It causes it.

Back right-to-counsel and tenant unions.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Medical bills

MEDICAL BILLS PUSHED 7.7 MILLION INTO POVERTY

Census, 2025. A diagnosis shouldn't come with an eviction notice.

Defend Medicaid. Fight for care for all.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
War on Poverty

THE WAR ON POVERTY WORKED

Poverty fell from about 26% to 16% from 1967 to 2012 on a consistent measure.

Finish the job. Fund what works.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Senior poverty history

35% IN 1959. 9.8% IN 2025.

Senior poverty, before and after Social Security and Medicare grew up.

Protect Social Security. Expand it.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Minimum wage

$15,080 A YEAR IS NOT A LIVING

That's $7.25 full time. Louisiana has no minimum wage of its own.

Demand a living wage in Louisiana.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Minimum wage CBO

A $15 FLOOR LIFTS 1.3 MILLION

CBO's estimate of people raised out of poverty by a $15 federal minimum.

Call Congress. Raise the wage.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Housing aid

HOUSING AID LIFTED 2.1 MILLION

Out of poverty in 2025. Most families who qualify still wait.

Demand housing vouchers for everyone who's eligible.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Renters

1 IN 4 RENTERS IS POOR

Renters' poverty rate hit 24% on the Census fuller measure in 2025.

Join or start a tenant union.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Child allowance

EVERY KID. EVERY MONTH.

A child allowance is the single biggest child poverty cut the experts found.

Make it permanent this time.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Louisiana kids

50TH FOR KIDS' ECONOMIC WELL-BEING

Louisiana's rank in the 2026 KIDS COUNT report. These babies deserve better.

Show up at the Capitol. Speak for Louisiana's kids.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Neighborhood poverty

20% OF LOUISIANA KIDS IN HIGH-POVERTY NEIGHBORHOODS

Nationally it's 7%. KIDS COUNT, 2024.

Fight for investment in every parish.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Hispanic poverty

PROGRESS IS POSSIBLE

Hispanic poverty hit a record low of 13.9% in 2025, down from 21.9% in 1973.

Keep the programs that made it happen.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Black poverty

7.9 MILLION BLACK AMERICANS IN POVERTY

A 17.3% rate in 2025. Not destiny. Policy.

Fight for wages, housing and a child allowance for all.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
SNAP losses

5 MILLION KNOCKED OFF FOOD AID

Estimated SNAP drop, July 2025 to May 2026. Over 1.5 million kids.

Help a neighbor reapply. Then call Congress.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
CTC left out

19 MILLION KIDS TOO POOR FOR A FULL CREDIT

The 2025 law still shortchanges the poorest children. CBPP.

Make the Child Tax Credit fully refundable.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Who's poor

POVERTY HAS EVERY FACE

White, Black, Latino, Asian, Native. Kids, workers, seniors. It's all of us.

Organize across every line they use to divide us.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Old line vs new line

$32,649 OR $41,700?

Official line vs. Census's fuller line for a renting family of four, 2025.

Measure poverty honestly. Then end it.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Rural South

NEARLY 1 IN 5 IN THE RURAL SOUTH

Southern nonmetro poverty ran 19.7% across 2015-19. USDA.

Organize your parish. Demand your share.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
We know how

WE KNOW HOW TO END IT

Social Security. SNAP. Child credits. Medicaid. Every one works.

Vote, organize and make them fund it.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Full-time work

FULL-TIME AND STILL POOR

Over a million full-time, year-round workers stayed below the line in 2025.

Raise the wage. Join a union.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Six dollars a day

SIX DOLLARS A DAY

Average SNAP benefit, 2025. Congress still cut it.

Defend SNAP. Call your senators.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Medicaid and poverty

MEDICAID KEEPS THE DOCTOR FROM TAKING THE RENT

Medical bills pushed millions into poverty in 2025. Medicaid stands in the way.

Stop the Medicaid cuts before 2027.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Gulf South

OIL BOOM. KID BUST.

1 in 4 Louisiana kids lived in poverty in 2024 while the petrochemical corridor boomed.

Make industry pay its share to Louisiana's children.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Spanish: Poverty is a policy choice

LA POBREZA ES UNA DECISIÓN POLÍTICA

En 2021, el crédito tributario por hijos sacó a 2.9 millones de niños de la pobreza.

Exige que el Congreso lo restablezca.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Spanish: SNAP

NADIE DEBE PASAR HAMBRE

SNAP sacó a 3.1 millones de personas de la pobreza en 2025.

Defiende SNAP. Llama a tus senadores.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Vietnamese: Poverty is a policy choice

NGHÈO ĐÓI LÀ MỘT LỰA CHỌN CHÍNH SÁCH

Năm 2021, tín thuế trẻ em đã giúp 2,9 triệu trẻ em thoát nghèo.

Hãy gọi cho dân biểu của bạn.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Closing poster

END POVERTY. ON PURPOSE.

We ended most senior poverty. We cut child poverty to a record low. Finish it.

Join us. Organize your block.

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Poverty is basically solved in America

Rebuttal: Poverty fell slightly in 2025, a real improvement. But Census still counted 34.5 million people below the official line, and 13.1% under the fuller measure.

Sources: Census 2025

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Record median income proves everyone is doing well

Rebuttal: Median income did hit a record, $87,460. But the top 1% hold about 31.6% of wealth while the bottom half holds 2.5%. Medians hide gaps.

Sources: Census 2025, Federal Reserve DFA

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Social Security is a failing program

Rebuttal: It faces a shortfall after 2034 under current law, a real issue. But it lifted 28.8 million people out of poverty in 2025. Lifting the payroll cap would close much of the gap.

Sources: Census 2025, SSA Trustees 2025

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: The expanded Child Tax Credit didn't help kids

Rebuttal: Census data show child poverty fell to a record 5.2% in 2021 with the expanded credit, then more than doubled to 12.4% when it expired.

Sources: Census SPM

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: The 2025 budget law helps working families

Rebuttal: Some families gain from tax provisions. But CBO found the bottom 10% lose about $1,200 a year on average while the top 10% gain about $13,600.

Sources: CBO 2025

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Corporate tax collections are healthy

Rebuttal: Corporate income tax receipts fell 23% in the first ten months of fiscal 2026, CBO reports, while individual income taxes rose 7%.

Sources: CBO MBR July 2026

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: We have to cut programs because of the debt

Rebuttal: Debt matters. But interest costs jumped partly because of tax cuts. Net interest hit $963 billion through July of fiscal 2026, more than defense. Revenue choices drive the debt too.

Sources: CBO MBR July 2026

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Tariffs are paid by foreign countries

Rebuttal: U.S. importers pay customs duties to the Treasury, and costs are often passed on to consumers. Duties brought in $154 billion through July of fiscal 2026.

Sources: CBO MBR July 2026

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: The job market is strong

Rebuttal: It was strong for years. But BLS reported only 29,000 jobs added in September 2026 and unemployment up to 4.2%, the highest since 2021.

Sources: BLS Employment Situation Sept 2026

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Anyone who wants a job can get one

Rebuttal: BLS counts 7.1 million unemployed and 4.5 million working part time who want full-time work. 1.9 million have been looking six months or more.

Sources: BLS Sept 2026

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Wages are rising fast

Rebuttal: Pay rose 3.0% over the year to September 2026. Prices rose 3.4% over the year to August. Real pay is slipping.

Sources: BLS

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Union membership is collapsing

Rebuttal: Membership held at 10.0% in 2025, with 14.7 million members, BLS says. Organizing continues despite heavy opposition.

Sources: BLS Union Members 2025

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Unions don't raise pay

Rebuttal: BLS data show union members earned a median $1,404 a week in 2025 vs. $1,174 for nonunion workers.

Sources: BLS Union Members 2025

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Workplaces are safe now

Rebuttal: Safety has improved over decades. But BLS counted 5,070 work deaths in 2024, one every 104 minutes.

Sources: BLS CFOI 2024

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Immigrant workers take the easy jobs

Rebuttal: BLS recorded 1,229 Hispanic or Latino work deaths in 2024, about two-thirds foreign-born. They often take the most dangerous jobs.

Sources: BLS CFOI 2024

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Americans are living longer, so health care is fine

Rebuttal: Life expectancy hit a record 79 in 2024, good news. But peer countries still live longer while spending less, and 26.7 million were uninsured in 2025.

Sources: CDC NCHS, Census 2025

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: The overdose crisis is over

Rebuttal: Deaths fell 26.2% in 2024, the biggest drop ever. But 79,384 people still died. Cutting treatment funding risks reversing progress.

Sources: CDC NCHS

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Families are financially healthy

Rebuttal: Some are. But household debt reached $18.8 trillion in mid-2026, with $1.26 trillion on credit cards.

Sources: NY Fed Q2 2026

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Homelessness is getting worse every year

Rebuttal: Not in 2025. HUD's count fell 3.4%, the first drop since 2016. But chronic homelessness hit a record. Honest data shows progress and pain.

Sources: HUD AHAR 2025

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Louisiana's economy is working for its people

Rebuttal: Louisiana had the highest poverty rate in the country, 19.7% over 2023–2025, nearly double the national rate.

Sources: Census

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Ending the hunger report saves money and avoids politics

Rebuttal: The report cost little and ran under both parties for nearly 30 years. Its final edition found 47.9 million people in food-insecure households in 2024. Dropping it hides a problem.

Sources: USDA ERS

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Disaster costs aren't rising

Rebuttal: NOAA logged 27 billion-dollar disasters in 2024 before retiring the database. The trend had been rising for decades.

Sources: NOAA NCEI

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Women and men are paid the same now

Rebuttal: Census found women working full time, year round earned 83.9 cents per man's dollar in 2025. The gap narrowed but persists.

Sources: Census 2025

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Tipped workers make plenty

Rebuttal: Some do. But the federal tipped minimum has been $2.13 an hour since 1991. Workers depend on customers for basic pay.

Sources: DOL

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: States should set their own wages

Rebuttal: States can. But five Southern states, including Louisiana, have no minimum wage law at all, leaving workers at $7.25.

Sources: DOL

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: The minimum wage is still a fair floor

Rebuttal: It's been $7.25 since 2009. Using BLS price data, it has lost roughly a third of its buying power (estimate).

Sources: DOL, BLS CPI

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Everyone pays Social Security tax the same way

Rebuttal: The tax stops at $184,500 in wages in 2026. A cashier pays on every dollar. A multimillionaire stops paying early in the year.

Sources: SSA

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Only the rich worry about the estate tax

Rebuttal: That's mostly true, and that's the point. The exemption is $15 million per person in 2026. Very few estates pay. It's a tax on dynasties.

Sources: 2025 law, JCT

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: High top tax rates kill growth

Rebuttal: The top rate was 91% for much of the 1950s, a time of strong growth. Growth depends on many things, but high top rates didn't stop it.

Sources: IRS historical tables

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: SNAP cuts only target fraud

Rebuttal: CBO estimated about $186 billion in SNAP cuts over ten years, mostly from work rules and state cost shifts, not fraud.

Sources: CBO 2025

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Child care is a private family issue

Rebuttal: Labor Department data show care for one child can cost 9% to 16% of median family income. It's an economic issue for every working parent.

Sources: DOL National Database of Childcare Prices

title: Claude Drop: publicdata-counter_argument
author: Claude
text:
Claim: Student debt is people's own choice

Rebuttal: People chose school, sure. But tuition rose far faster than wages. Total student debt is $1.65 trillion, held by about 42 million federal borrowers.

Sources: NY Fed, Dept. of Education
